Thus we should move the queen. The candidate moves are checks: Qe3+, Qe5+, Qb3+ and quiet moves: Qe4, Qf5, Qd5, Qf6, etc.

We want to minimize the opponent's best options. Qe3+ gives two safe squares: g2 and h2. Qe5+ gives four. Qb3+ gives three. Quiet moves like Qe4 give three safe squares (f2, h2, h3). But note that after Qe4, the king is not in check, but it's forced to move because it has moves? It's not forced, it can stay? No, in chess you must move. But the king is not in check, so it's not forced to move? Actually, any legal move is allowed. Black has legal moves: f2, h2, h3. So it must move one of its pieces. It only has a king, so it must move the king to one of those squares. So it's not "forced" in the sense of check, but it must move the king. So it will move to f2, h2, or h3. Qe3+ forces the king to g2 or h2 because it's check and the other squares are attacked. So after Qe3+, we know exactly where it goes: g2 or h2. After Qe4, it can go to f2, h2, h3. So Qe3+ is more restrictive and forces the king closer to the edge (g2 and h2 are edge-adjacent; f2 is not edge, h3 is not edge). So Qe3+ seems better.
